Q2.answer:
(a) **Abbott**: performance 7+5+5 = **17**; preference **0**; total **17**. **Bianchi**: 5+0+3 = **8**; 30%+ disabled preference **+5**; total **13** (351.503(a), (f); 351.504(a)(1)). **Castillo**: 7+5+5 = **17**; not a preference eligible (length-of-service retirement after 22 years; no disability; 351.504(b)(1)–(4)); **0**; total **17**. **Dalton**: two ratings 5 and 2 = 7+0 = 7; proxy (7+0)/2 = **3.5**; performance **10.5**; preference **+3**; total **13.5** (351.503(f)(2); 351.504(a)(2)). **Eze**: 5+5+5 = **15**; preference **0**; total **15**; term appointment of four years is not excluded by 351.202(d)(2)(iii) and is subgroup II under 351.502(a)(3). **Fontaine**: one rating Level 4 = 5 × 3 = **15**; preference **0**; total **15** (351.503(f)(3)).
(b) Order: **Abbott (17)** over Castillo (17) by earlier SCD (May 1, 2003 vs. Aug. 1, 2012), both subgroup I (351.501(c)); **Fontaine (15)** over Eze (15) because Fontaine is subgroup I and Eze subgroup II (351.501(c)); then **Eze (15)**; then **Dalton (13.5)**; then **Bianchi (13)**. Released: **Dalton and Bianchi**.
(c) Under the earlier rules Bianchi would have stood **above Abbott**: employees were ranked first by tenure group I/II/III, then within the group by veterans’ preference subgroup AD, A, B, and only then by adjusted SCD/performance; Bianchi’s AD subgroup outranked Abbott’s B subgroup regardless of performance or service (91 FR 49198).
(d) Bianchi may review the complete retention register for her competitive level, including the names of all employees on it, their performance credit as augmented by veterans’ preference, and their SCDs, and the registers for other positions that could affect the composition of her competitive level or her assignment rights (5 CFR 351.506(c)(1)–(2); 351.506(b)).

Q3.answer:
(a) **A**: not a preference eligible; **0 points**; Subgroup **B**. 351.504(b)(1) not met (length-of-service retirement, no disability); (b)(2) not met (22 years); (b)(3) not met; (b)(4) fails because not a disabled veteran. **B**: not a preference eligible; **0 points**; Subgroup **B**. Retirement pay is based on 21 years’ active service, so (b)(2) is not met; (b)(1) is not met because retirement is not based on disability; (b)(4) requires meeting (b)(1)–(3). **C**: preference eligible; **5 points**; Subgroup **AD**. Disability retirement for injury in the line of duty as a direct result of armed conflict satisfies 351.504(b)(1), and major is “major or above” under (b)(4). **D**: not a preference eligible; **0 points**; Subgroup **B**. 351.504(b)(2) not met (24 years), rank below major, no disability. **E**: preference eligible; **3 points**; Subgroup **A**. Although the 10% disability is not from armed conflict or an instrumentality of war, retired pay is not based on 20 or more years of full-time active service, so 351.504(b)(2) is met; because the disability is under 30%, 351.504(a)(2) gives 3 points.
(b) **A**: not a preference eligible, so under 351.505(b)(2)(i) only the 2 years of campaign-badge service count; SCD = Sept. 7, 2010 − 2 years = **Sept. 7, 2008**. **C**: preference eligible, so 351.505(b)(2)(ii) credits total active service (14 years); SCD = Sept. 7, 2010 − 14 years = **Sept. 7, 1996**.
(c) The AD/A/B subgroups do not independently order retention. Veterans’ preference operates only through the 5/3/0 points added to performance credit; subgroup labels are recorded on the register and notice. Tenure subgroup I/II is a tie-breaker only after augmented performance credit ties, and SCD breaks remaining ties (351.501(b)–(c), 351.504(a)).

Q4.answer:

Q5.answer:
(a)(i) Notice **Aug. 28, 2026** is before Sept. 2, so the earlier rules apply (91 FR 49178, 49207). Under them, Level 5 = 20 years and Level 3 = 12 years additional service; Lee: (12+12+12)/3 = 12 years, adjusted SCD Mar. 2, 1986; Park: (20+20+20)/3 = 20 years, adjusted SCD July 8, 1999. Both are Group I/Subgroup B; earlier adjusted SCD wins, so **Park is released**. (ii) Notice **Sept. 2, 2026** is on the effective date, so the amended rules apply: Lee 3+3+3 = **9**; Park 7+7+7 = **21**; **Lee is released**. (iii) Notice **Sept. 3, 2026**: same amended rules; **Lee is released**.
(b) **No recalculation.** The Sept. 3 notice fixed retention standing as of receipt (351.507(a)). An amended notice solely moving the effective date to a later date is not a new specific RIF notice and does not require redetermination or recalculation of retention standing under subpart E (351.805(b)). Lee’s Oct. 15 Level 5 rating therefore does not change the result; Lee remains released.
(c) (1) **Which version applies**: the date the agency **issues** the RIF notice — DATES, 91 FR 49178, and Implementation, 91 FR 49207. (2) **End of the four-year ratings period**: the date of issuance of RIF notices, or the agency’s cutoff date if one is used — 351.503(c)(1)–(2). (3) **Tenure subgroup and retention standing**: the date the employee **receives** a specific RIF notice — 351.502(a)(2)–(3), (b)(2)–(3); 351.507(a).

Q6.answer:
(a) Jordan has assignment rights to positions **1 (GS-12 Ellis)**, **2 (GS-11 Frank)**, and **3 (GS-10 Gale)**: each is in the same competitive area, has the same full-time work schedule, is held by an employee with lower retention standing in the same tenure group, and is within three grades of GS-13 (351.701(a), (b)). The agency **must offer position 1**, because it requires the least reduction in representative rate. Position 4 (GS-9) is four grades below GS-13, outside the three-grade limit; position 5 (Ito) is held by a higher-standing employee; position 6 (Kim) is part-time, not the same type of work schedule; position 7 (Lund) is in a different competitive area.
(b) With a compensable 30%+ disability, the grade limit becomes **five grades**, so position 4 (GS-9) also becomes within reach (351.701(b)(2)); the mandatory offer is still **position 1**, the least reduction.
(c) If Jordan’s current annual rating is **Level 1**, 351.701(a) does not apply: only an employee with a current annual rating of Level 2 or higher has assignment rights. He has **no assignment right** to any of the positions.
(d) In the excepted service, 351.701 does not apply by its terms (it covers a “competitive service tenure group employee”). An agency may, in its discretion, adopt provisions giving excepted-service employees assignment rights on the same basis under 351.705(a); absent such agency action, there is **no mandatory assignment right**.
(e) The handbook’s “Level 2 cannot take a position held by someone with a higher rating” statement reflects the former Sec. 351.701(d), which the final rule **eliminated** because it was no longer necessary; 351.701(a) now permits assignment for a Level 2 or higher employee, subject to the other requirements (91 FR 49204). The separate “bumping” and “retreating” concepts were also replaced: assignment rights now run to a position held by an employee with lower retention standing in the same tenure group, without the old bump/retreat distinction (91 FR 49204; 351.701(b)).

Q7.answer:
(a) **The Merit Systems Protection Board** hears the appeal. The OPM appeals rule applies only to a RIF action for which the agency issues a specific RIF notice under 351.802 **on or after Sept. 2, 2026** (2026-15666, DATES, 91 FR 49230). The MSPB’s Appellate Jurisdiction Update II (2026-16456) is effective Sept. 2, 2026 but states that MSPB will continue to adjudicate RIF appeals relating to actions taken before that date, including cases where the RIF notice was issued before the rule’s effective date (91 FR 51997–51998). The proposed appeals rule (2026-02576) is not authority.
(b) **OPM** hears the appeal. Morgan must file through the electronic filing system identified on OPM’s website (351.902(a)). Deadline: 30 calendar days from the Dec. 18, 2026 effective date; the first day counted is Dec. 19, 2026; the 30th day is Sunday, Jan. 17, 2027; Jan. 18, 2027 is the Martin Luther King, Jr. Federal holiday; the first workday is **Tuesday, Jan. 19, 2027**, and the appeal is timely if e-filed by **11:59 p.m. Eastern Time** that day (351.902(b), (b)(1)).
(c) She must prove by a preponderance of the evidence: timeliness; OPM jurisdiction; that the agency failed to comply with an applicable statute or OPM RIF regulation; and that the failure prejudiced her by causing the appealed action or the loss of a materially more favorable outcome (351.901(b)). She is **not entitled to a hearing as of right**; review is on the written record unless OPM determines a hearing is “necessary and efficient” (351.905(c)).
(d) The rule bars the union’s grievance: a RIF action and any matter relating to an appeal of it “may not be raised under a negotiated grievance procedure or contested through grievance arbitration” (351.901(c)(2)). The preamble says the final rule does **not retroactively invalidate existing CBAs** or adjudicate particular CBA disputes; OPM does not adopt the position that the proposal would automatically vitiate existing agreements mid-term; when agreements are renegotiated, the governmentwide rule will limit bargaining for a direct RIF appeal process inconsistent with part 351; questions about particular existing agreement provisions, negotiability disputes, or unfair-labor-practice allegations remain for resolution under chapter 71 (91 FR 49245).
(e) **No.** A party cannot obtain judicial review of a decision under subpart I (351.901(c)(4)); there is no further right of appeal of a final OPM decision (351.909(e)); the preamble explains the CSRA exclusivity (91 FR 49242–49243).
(f) **Yes.** Because she timely filed an OSC complaint before the RIF appeal period expired and the final decision on that matter materially affects her retention standing, she may file a RIF appeal within 30 calendar days after the decision becomes final and no longer subject to further administrative review (351.902(b)(3)). The March 10, 2027 final decision gives a deadline of **April 9, 2027** (March 11 is day 1; April 9 is day 30), e-filed by 11:59 p.m. ET. OPM determines in its sole discretion whether the decision materially affects her rights.
(g) The controlling provision is the **DATES** sentence of 2026-15666 at **91 FR 49230**: “This final rule applies only to a RIF action for which an agency issues the employee a specific RIF notice under 5 CFR 351.802 on or after September 2, 2026.”

Q8.answer:
(a) **Today (Nov. 14, 2026)**, 5 CFR 351.806 is the pre-amendment version, which OPM describes as using “when possible” for the duty-status presumption; the 2026 documents do not print its full current text (the preamble at 91 FR 65925–65926 and 65933 describes the change from “when possible” to “under ordinary circumstances”). **Adopted but not yet in force**: 2026-21320, effective **Nov. 18, 2026**, revises 351.806 to read: (a) under ordinary circumstances an employee remains in duty status during the notice period; (b) nothing precludes an agency from placing an employee on administrative leave for all or part of the notice period when appropriate and consistent with part 630, subpart N; (c) emergency lack of work or funds permits annual leave with or without consent, leave without pay with consent, or nonpay status without consent (91 FR 65939).
(b) **No employee consent is required** to place an employee on administrative leave under 351.806(b); the preamble says “provide” covers administrative leave “with or without the employee’s consent” (91 FR 65933). Neither 351.806(b) nor the companion 630.1403(c)(10) states a fixed maximum duration; the leave must satisfy subpart N’s general principles (including 630.1403(a)(3): usually not more than one workday, longer only when appropriate). OPM’s governmentwide policy limit of 12 weeks per instance for administrative leave in connection with a workforce realignment initiative is discussed in the preamble (91 FR 65926, 65935), but 630.1403(c)(10) does not expressly incorporate it.
(c) OPM says its policy guidance — section D.1.b of the Agency Policy Template (CPM 2025-12, July 30, 2025) — already provided that an authorized agency official may provide administrative leave between an employee’s receipt of a notice of involuntary separation and the effective date of separation; the rule merely codifies that existing guidance (91 FR 65926 & n.3).
(d) **No.** OPM states that the new 630.1403(c)(10) and revised 351.806 address only paid non-duty status and do not alter RIF competition, retention registers, retention standing, veterans’ preference, notice, or appeal rights; nothing authorizes bypassing RIF procedures (91 FR 65926).
Q8.uncertainty: The exact full text of the current pre-Nov. 18 version of 351.806 is not printed; also, whether the 12-week policy limit applies to RIF-notice administrative leave under 630.1403(c)(10) is not expressly resolved.

Q9.answer:
**In order: Steps 2, 7 and 9.** **Do not comply: Steps 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 11 and 12.**
- **Step 1 — noncompliant.** The Tulsa Field Office is an organizational unit on the official chart and was approved by the agency head’s designee, which is permitted, but it was established **Aug. 17, 2026**, fewer than 90 days before the **Oct. 13, 2026** notices. The agency therefore had to submit a description and written statement of bona fide organizational basis to OPM for approval in advance; nothing was sent (351.402(b)(1), (c)).
- **Step 2 — in order.** A career-conditional employee serving the initial probationary period is not a competing employee and may be retained while a competing employee is released (351.202(d)(2)(ii), (d)(3)).
- **Step 3 — noncompliant.** A supervisory probationary period is not an “initial probationary period” (351.203, definition), so Ms. Ortiz must be included and ranked in competitive service tenure subgroup I; the agency must not omit her merely because she is on supervisory probation.
- **Step 4 — noncompliant.** The 30-day cutoff was **Sept. 13, 2026**; the Oct. 2, 2026 rating was received after the cutoff and cannot be used. The agency also violated the uniform-and-consistent requirement by using a later rating for only one employee (351.503(c)(2), (c)(3), (c)(4)).
- **Step 5 — noncompliant.** For two ratings, the missing-rating proxy is (7+5)/2 = **6**, so Ms. Quist’s credit is 7+5+6 = **18**, not 15 (351.503(f)(2)).
- **Step 6 — noncompliant.** Additional points for performance are permitted only under the single-rating-pattern rule for a pattern whose highest level is Level 3, and only for documented exceptional performance; they are not authorized as a 2-point add-on for QSI recipients under a five-level pattern (351.503(d), (e)).
- **Step 7 — in order.** When employees are tied on augmented performance credit, tenure subgroup and SCD, the agency may select any tied employee for release (351.601(c)).
- **Step 8 — noncompliant.** The agency may not release a competing employee from a competitive level while retaining an employee in that level with a specifically limited temporary or term promotion (351.602(a)).
- **Step 9 — in order.** No new assessment is required where, during the five years ending on the date the employee receives the specific RIF notice, the employee held the same position (or same grade/pay level with substantially the same duties, series, qualifications and conditions) and received a Level 3 or higher rating for those duties (351.702(a)(4)(v)).
- **Step 10 — noncompliant.** An assessment may not consist solely of, or principally rely on, an automated self-assessment; the agency must use a job-analysis-based assessment allowing demonstration of job-related skills, abilities, knowledge and competencies (351.702(a)(4)(i)–(iii)).
- **Step 11 — noncompliant.** Temporary exceptions may not be sequenced or stacked; the agency may use one exception, and if more than one is available, the one providing the longest retention, not 60 days plus another 60 days (351.608(a)(3); 351.608(b) and (g) each allow up to 90 days).
- **Step 12 — noncompliant.** For a RIF noticed on Oct. 13, 2026, the appeal is to **OPM**, not MSPB. The notice must state the right to appeal to OPM, the time limit under 351.902(b), and the electronic filing system (351.802(a)(6), as amended by 2026-15666; 351.901).

Q10.answer:
(a) On **Sept. 10, 2026**, paragraph (1) of the definition of “displaced” in 5 CFR 330.602 contained **only the introductory text** — “A current competitive service employee in the competitive service tenure group at grade GS-15 (or equivalent) or below (or another qualifying competitive service appointment, as determined by OPM) who:” — with **no subparagraphs (i) or (ii)**. Amendatory instruction 11 of 2026-15665 set out only the introductory text as the revised paragraph, which inadvertently deleted (1)(i) and (1)(ii).
(b) **2026-18800**, published and effective **Sept. 15, 2026**, restored paragraphs (1)(i) and (1)(ii) as they read before the final rule. OPM acted without notice and comment under the good-cause exception of **5 U.S.C. 553(b)(B)**, stating that the correction makes **no substantive change** — it restores text in effect before Sept. 2, 2026 that OPM did not propose to remove and the final rule did not discuss removing — and made it effective upon publication under 553(d)(3) (91 FR 58363–58364).
(c) After the correction, under paragraph (1)(i): if Nadia is offered a full-time position with a **lower** representative rate than her present full-time position and declines, she has **not** declined an offer of a position with the same type of work schedule and a representative rate at least as high as her present position, so she **remains “displaced.”** If the offered position had the **same** representative rate (and same work schedule), declining it would mean she has declined a qualifying offer, and she would **not** be “displaced” under paragraph (1)(i).

Q11.answer:
Real differences between the proposed and final part 351 regulatory text (paragraph; proposed → final):
1. **351.202(d)(2)(iii)**: proposed excluded a “temporary or term appointment of 1 year or less under subpart C or D of part 316”; final excludes only “a temporary appointment of one (1) year or less under subpart D of part 316.”
2. **351.202(d)(3)–(4)**: proposed said covered employees “may be retained, furloughed, separated, demoted or reassigned without regard to the provisions of this part”; final states they are not competing employees, specifies the actions may be taken without retention-standing/order-of-release/assignment-right determinations, and adds (d)(4), requiring a modified notice under 351.801 with specified 351.802 content.
3. **351.203 “Furlough”**: proposed added “and is instead dependent entirely on congressional action, rather than agency action”; final omits that clause.
4. **351.203 “Rating of record”**: proposed cross-referenced Sec. 430.208(d); final cross-references Sec. 430.208(e).
5. **351.204**: proposed required only following/applying the regulations; final adds the responsibility to ensure they are administered and applied consistent with all applicable laws, including the merit system principles in 5 U.S.C. 2301(b).
6. **351.302(d)**: proposed required use of part 752 adverse-action procedures; final adds “or other procedures required by law, regulation, or the terms of the employee’s appointment.”
7. **351.402**: proposed revised only paragraph (b); final also revises paragraph (c), adding the requirement to submit a competitive-area description and bona fide organizational explanation to OPM for approval when a competitive area is established or materially modified within 90 days before specific RIF notices.
8. **351.502**: proposed measured tenure subgroup status “as of the date the agency issues a specific reduction in force notice”; final measures it “as of the date the employee receives a specific reduction in force notice” (subgroup I and II, competitive and excepted).
9. **351.502(a)(3)**: proposed excluded a “temporary or time-limited appointment of 1 year or less under subpart C or D of part 316”; final excludes only “a temporary appointment of 1 year or less under subpart D of part 316.”
10. **351.503(a)(1)**: proposed referenced “patterns of summary level in Sec. 430.208(d)”; final references “5 CFR 430.208(e).”
11. **351.503(d) and (e)(2)**: final adds the authorization clause for pattern A/pass-fail or pattern D systems “authorized under [Sec. 430.208(d)] prior to the final rule prescribed at 91 FR 41521” (as corrected by 2026-17335); proposed had no such clause.
12. **351.504(a)**: proposed said the AD/A/B subgroups “should be identified”; final says “must be identified.”
13. **351.505(b)(2)**: proposed said “a retired member … covered by Sec. 351.503(b)”; final says “covered by Sec. 351.504(b).”
14. **351.506(c)(2)**: proposed cross-referenced “Sec. 351.701(b) and (c)”; final, as corrected, cross-references only “Sec. 351.701(b).”
15. **351.506(d)**: final adds that an employee who has not received a specific RIF notice has no right under the section, but that this does not limit access under another statute or regulation; proposed had no such sentence.
16. **351.604**: proposed would have revised paragraph (b) and removed paragraph (d) (RIF furlough criteria); final did not adopt those amendments.
17. **351.605**: proposed combined the abolishment rule and notice in paragraph (b); final restructures into (a) appropriate use, (b) abolishment, (c) notice (with a written notice under 351.801 and identification of the competitive area being abolished), and (d) retention register not required (and “must not” apply assignment rights).
18. **351.606(a)**: proposed gave a general retention priority under Sec. 351.209(b); final adds detailed mandatory-exception rules in (a)(1)–(6), including first determining ordinary retention standing, reassignment when an entire competitive area is abolished, OPM placement assistance, and documentation.
19. **351.608(a)(2)**: proposed cross-referenced CTAP at part 330, subpart E; final cross-references subpart F.
20. **351.702(a)(4)**: final adds paragraph (v), the exception from the assessment requirement for an employee who held the same or substantially similar position within five years and received a Level 3 or higher rating; proposed had no equivalent.
21. **351.802**: final adds introductory text to paragraph (a) and changes proposed “veteran status” to “veterans’ preference subgroup,” and proposed “A link to part 351 … and access to the agency’s records” to “A link to 5 CFR part 351 and information on how to access the agency’s records.”
22. **351.805(b)**: final adds the rule that an amended notice solely stating a later effective date is not a new specific RIF notice and does not require redetermination/recalculation of retention standing; proposed contained no such amendment.
Q11.uncertainty: The list covers differences I could verify from the printed regulatory text; it omits purely stylistic changes and may not capture every non-substantive wording change.

Q12.answer:
(a) **Register (GS-13 level):**
- **Alvarez**: 7+7+5 = **19**; preference 0; total **19**; career = subgroup I.
- **Chen**: the Sept. 30, 2022 Level 2 is outside the four-year period beginning Oct. 5, 2022; two ratings remain, Nov. 14, 2024 Level 5 (7) and Nov. 13, 2025 Level 4 (5); proxy = (7+5)/2 = 6; credit = **18**; preference 0; total **18**; subgroup I.
- **Dube**: 5+5 = 10; proxy = 5; performance 15; preference +3; total **18**; career-conditional after probation = subgroup II.
- **Estrada**: the Oct. 20, 2026 Level 5 is after the Oct. 5 notice and is not used; ratings Nov. 2023 Level 4 (5), Nov. 2024 Level 3 (3), Nov. 2025 Level 4 (5) = 13; preference +3; total **16**; subgroup I.
- **Brandt**: 3+5+0 = 8; 30%+ disabled preference +5; total **13**; subgroup I.
- **Farouk**: one actual rating Level 3; 3 × 3 = **9**; preference 0; total **9**; subgroup I. He is a **restoration protected employee** (restored July 13, 2026; 14 months’ uniformed service gives a one-year protection period under 38 U.S.C. 4316(c) and 351.203), so the mandatory exception in 351.606(a) applies.
- **Quinn**: **not on the register** — career-conditional serving the initial probationary period, excluded from RIF competition by 351.202(d)(2)(ii).
Order of retention: **Alvarez (19) > Chen (18, subgroup I) > Dube (18, subgroup II) > Estrada (16) > Brandt (13) > Farouk (9)**. Chen outranks Dube because both have 18 and subgroup I is ahead of subgroup II (351.501(c)).
(b) The three released are **Brandt, Estrada and Dube**, not Farouk. Farouk has the lowest score (9), but as a restoration protected employee he may not be released from the competitive level while another competing employee may be released instead (351.606(a)(2)); the agency must retain him and release the next lowest employees. Brandt is next lowest at 13; Estrada at 16; Dube at 18 (Dube is below Chen at the same 18 because Dube is subgroup II).
(c) **Brandt** (30%+ disabled; five-grade limit) has lower standing than Gomez (17), Hill (14) and Jones (15), but higher than Ikeda (9); he must be offered **Ikeda’s GS-9** position. **Estrada** (three-grade limit: GS-12, GS-11, GS-10) has lower standing than Gomez (17), but higher than Hill (14), Jones (15) and Ikeda (9); he must be offered **Hill’s GS-11**, the least reduction (not Jones’s GS-10). **Dube** has 18, higher than Gomez’s 17, so he must be offered **Gomez’s GS-12**, the least reduction. Dube cannot displace Chen (same 18 but Chen subgroup I), and Brandt cannot reach Gomez/Hill/Jones because their standing is higher.
(d) If all offers are accepted, the GS-13 employees remain; the displaced holders **Gomez, Hill and Ikeda** are released from their one-position competitive levels and, being qualified only for the positions they held, have no assignment rights and are **separated**.
Q12.uncertainty: Assumes Farouk’s 14 months of uniformed service is more than 180 days, giving a one-year protection period; even on the shorter six-month period, he would still be within protection on Oct. 5, 2026.

Q13.answer:
Preamble statements in 2026-15665 that differ from its own regulatory text:
1. **Erosion-of-duties amendment**: preamble at **91 FR 49190** says OPM is modifying **Sec. 351.201(a)(2)** to remove erosion-of-duties reclassifications “if the action would take effect after an agency had formally announced a RIF … and the RIF would take effect within 180 days.” The regulatory text instead amends **Sec. 351.202(c)(3)** at **91 FR 49218**, barring such a reclassification between formal announcement and completion of the RIF if it “would adversely affect an employee’s retention standing” — no 180-day condition. Another passage at **91 FR 49191** states the adverse-effect trigger correctly.
2. **Competitive-service temporary/time-limited exclusions**: preamble at **91 FR 49191** says “competitive and excepted service employees who are serving temporary or time-limited appointments of 1 year or less would be excluded from RIF competition.” The text at **91 FR 49218** (351.202(d)(2)(iii)) excludes only a **temporary** appointment of one year or less under part 316 subpart D for the competitive service; time-limited appointments are excluded only in the excepted service (351.202(d)(1)(i)). Another passage at **91 FR 49191** correctly notes that the final rule removed the proposed reference to term appointments and limits the competitive-service exclusion to temporary appointments under subpart D.
3. **Tenure group descriptions**: preamble at **91 FR 49196** says the competitive service tenure group excludes employees “as of the date of the RIF notice” serving “a temporary or time-limited appointment of 1 year or less,” and that subgroup II covers those not serving “a temporary or term appointment of 1 year or less.” The text at **91 FR 49220** measures status “as of the date the employee receives a specific reduction in force notice” and excludes only “a temporary appointment of 1 year or less under subpart D.” Another passage at **91 FR 49196** correctly uses “the date the employee receives a specific reduction in force notice” for subgroup I.
4. **“Preference eligible veteran”**: preamble at **91 FR 49197** says “each preference eligible veteran” receives 5 points and “every other preference eligible veteran” receives 3 points. The text at **91 FR 49221** (351.504(a)) applies to each “preference eligible employee” and every other “preference eligible employee”; preference eligibles include certain non-veteran family members. Another passage at **91 FR 49198** correctly notes that “preference eligibles” includes certain close family members of deceased or service-disabled veterans.
5. **Order of factors in examples**: preamble at **91 FR 49200** describes the final-rule order as “Tenure | Performance based on the total of the employee’s summary levels | Vets Pref | Service Computation Date.” The text at **91 FR 49220** (351.501(b)–(c)) makes performance credit **as augmented by veterans’ preference** the ranking factor, then uses tenure subgroup and SCD as tie-breakers. Another passage at **91 FR 49199** states that correctly.
6. **351.602 — appointment vs. promotion**: preamble at **91 FR 49202** says OPM is modifying Sec. 351.602 “to remove the prohibition on retaining an employee serving a specifically limited temporary appointment in a competitive level while releasing a competing employee.” The printed text at **91 FR 49223** still prohibits releasing a competing employee while retaining an employee with “a specifically limited temporary or term **promotion**.” No other passage states the point correctly.
7. **Grade limit for assignment rights**: preamble at **91 FR 49204** says a released employee has assignment rights to a position “not more than three grades below” the position from which released. The text at **91 FR 49225** (351.701(b)(2)) provides a **five-grade** limit for a preference eligible with a compensable service-connected disability of 30 percent or more. The Executive Summary at **91 FR 49178** states the five-grade exception correctly.
8. **Assessment exception — position and period**: Executive Summary item 13 at **91 FR 49178** says the assessment exception applies if the employee held “the same or substantially similar position within five years of the RIF” and received a Level 3 rating “for performing the duties of the position.” The text at **91 FR 49226** (351.702(a)(4)(v)) requires that, “during the 5-year period ending on the date the employee receives a specific reduction in force notice,” the employee occupied the same position, or a position at the same grade or pay level with substantially the same duties, occupational series, qualification requirements, and conditions, and received Level 3 or higher for those duties. Another passage at **91 FR 49204–49205** states the text accurately.
Q13.uncertainty: Some preamble statements are summaries rather than operative rules; I have listed only differences I could verify against the printed regulatory text.

Q14.answer:
(i) **Preamble vs. regulatory text of the OPM appeals rule**:
1. **Burden of proof — “required form”**: the preamble says the appellant must prove “that the written appeal was timely and in the required form” (**91 FR 49248**). The text, 351.901(b)(1) (**91 FR 49263**), requires proof only of “[t]he timeliness of the written appeal,” with no separate “required form” element.
2. **Inspection of the appellate record — omitted privileges**: the preamble says inspection is subject to the Privacy Act, classified-information/national-security requirements, protective orders, and “any other applicable limitation required by law” (**91 FR 49250**). The text, 351.903(d) (**91 FR 49265**), also subjects inspection to **applicable legal privileges**, which the preamble omits.
3. **Service — cross-reference to paragraph (b)**: the preamble says service is “subject to the disclosure limitations in paragraph (b)” (**91 FR 49250**). The text, 351.903(e) (**91 FR 49265**), does not cross-reference paragraph (b); it sets out its own list (Privacy Act, applicable legal privileges, classified/national-security requirements, OPM protective orders, and any other applicable disclosure limitation).
4. **“Responsible agency” in representation**: the preamble says OPM or the “responsible agency” may disallow a representative who is an employee of the “responsible agency or OPM” (**91 FR 49250**). As corrected, 351.904(c) (**91 FR 54796**) says “OPM or the agency whose action is under appeal” and “an employee of that agency or OPM”; the correction explains that “responsible agency” is undefined in part 351.
(ii) **Proposed-to-final changes not acknowledged in the summary near the start of the final preamble**:
1. **Removal of the FLRA from the preserved collateral forums**: proposed 351.901(c) preserved matters within the jurisdiction of the EEOC, **Federal Labor Relations Authority**, Inspector General, MSPB, DOL VETS and OSC (**91 FR 5875**). Final 351.901(c)(3) omits the FLRA and lists EEOC, Inspector General, MSPB, DOL VETS and OSC (**91 FR 49264**). The summary of changes discusses exclusivity and lists the preserved entities but does not acknowledge that the FLRA was dropped.
2. **Sanctions changed from mandatory to discretionary**: proposed 351.906(b) said OPM “shall” impose the listed consequences for failure to comply with a directive (**91 FR 5877**); final 351.906(b) says OPM “may” impose them (**91 FR 49266**). The summary’s “Refining protective-order authority” paragraph does not mention this change.
3. **E-filing exemption cross-reference added**: proposed 351.902(c)(2) barred filing/access unless registered as an e-filer; final 351.902(c)(2) adds “or exempted under paragraph (c)(7) of this section for good cause” (**91 FR 49264**). The summary’s e-filing discussion does not acknowledge this addition.
(iii) **Board/OPM inconsistency about which RIF appeals MSPB will still hear**:
1. **Within the Board’s rule**: the DATES and section I.B say MSPB will accept RIF appeals “where the agency’s RIF notice was issued before the rule’s effective date” (**91 FR 51997**), while section III says MSPB will adjudicate RIF appeals “in which the RIF effective date preceded September 2, 2026” (**91 FR 51998**) — a notice-date trigger in one place and an effective-date trigger in another.
2. **Between the Board and OPM**: OPM’s applicability turns on whether the agency **issued the specific RIF notice** on or after Sept. 2, 2026 (**2026-15666 DATES, 91 FR 49230**); the Board’s section III uses the **RIF effective date** (**91 FR 51998**). The Board’s DATES phrase “agency actions taken before the effective date” (**91 FR 51997**) is also ambiguous between notice issuance and RIF effectiveness.
Q14.uncertainty: The preamble-vs-text items are drafting inconsistencies; OPM may treat the regulatory text as controlling. The Board’s rule does not resolve whether the notice date or the RIF effective date controls for its retained cases.
